answer: Because the orchard height is fixed at intake and published in the raven receipt, the horizon audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 803 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. That is 21 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
